reason: The v43 receipt route intentionally carries Explorer-origin and Platform-origin profiles, but HRIS_CONFIG_AUTHOR qualifies for both. Auth evaluates the higher-precedence Explorer profile before the owner service can inspect the sealed receipt family, so a dual-qualified actor receives an Explorer route proof and cannot satisfy R4's forwarded Platform source-scope requirement. Static review also proved that the utility shell capability currently projects a matched responsibility as RESOURCE_SET although the R4 People contract requires SELF/SELF, and that Gateway-parity 63-bit authority revisions cannot be exposed through the JavaScript-safe public receipt fields. R5 closes these three coupled blockers without adding a public selector or widening People.
provenBlockingChain: route.hcm.utility.explorer-command-receipt.data has Explorer-origin precedence 350 and Platform-origin precedence 300.
HRIS_CONFIG_AUTHOR belongs to both the Explorer package set and the Platform receipt package set and may hold both required capabilities.
Auth and Gateway do not possess the owner receipt predicate evidence when they choose the route profile, so the higher-precedence Explorer profile wins for the overlapping actor.
The browser possesses only the current People-derived hcm-scope selected for the Explorer page; the activity projection deliberately exposes no authority selector or source payload.
A new public profile carrier alone would not solve the precedence conflict and would broaden Gateway, generated-contract and browser trust boundaries.

Platform can safely close the gap with the existing contextScopeKey contract: validate the forwarded coarse route first, inspect only the sealed receipt family internally, derive the exact canonical Auth source scope for ORIGINATING_COMMAND_SCOPE, and request exact lower-profile selection server-side before any Platform receipt is returned.

For hcm.utility hcm.app.shell.view, Auth currently validates the REQUIRED responsibility and then emits RESOURCE_SET scopes; R4 People intentionally accepts only exact SELF/SELF utility scope, so the Explorer proof is otherwise impossible.

Gateway derives field-policy and authorization authority revisions as positive 63-bit values, while the existing public receipt contract is parsed as JavaScript safe integers. Reusing one column for both authority and public transport either weakens Gateway parity or breaks the browser contract.

hcmUtilityShellSelfProjection.exactBoundary: Only when product=hcm, surface=hcm.utility and the evaluated capability is hcm.app.shell.view with scopeResolver SELF, Auth must continue to require and validate the configured responsibility, preserve its responsibility metadata and validTo freshness, but project exactly one SELF scope and bind every returned grant scopeKeys list to that same SELF key.
hcmUtilityShellSelfProjection.implementationConstraint: ProductAuthorizationAuthoritySupport.capabilityGrants currently rebuilds RESOURCE_SET keys when roles are present. Close the exception inside ProductAuthorizationAuthorityAdapter by exact post-evaluation scope-and-grant rebinding or an equivalently local branch; no edit outside the one authorized Auth production file is permitted.
hcmUtilityShellSelfProjection.noExpansion: The responsibility remains qualification evidence, not a population grant. No other product, surface, capability, resolver or responsibility-backed route changes, and People remains exact SELF/SELF with no RESOURCE_SET fallback.

authExactReceiptProfileSelector.selectorContract: Only for a direct evaluation of the exact receipt route, a canonical source scope matching ^scope-[a-f0-9]{32}$ may select the access profile whose evaluated single scope has that exact key. An allowed higher-precedence profile with a different source scope is skipped; if no allowed profile matches, return SCOPE_INVALID.
authExactReceiptProfileSelector.platformScopeMaterial: Use the existing ProductSurfaceScopeKey contract with the current tenant, actor, product hcm, surface hcm.utility, source ORIGINATING_COMMAND_SCOPE and kind TARGET_POPULATION. Platform derives the selector server-side; no browser profile label is trusted.
authExactReceiptProfileSelector.preservationRule: An absent selector or a People-derived hcm-scope preserves existing precedence and People eligibility. No other route gains profile selection and no profile key, capability, scope resolver, package, predicate or generated carrier changes.

twoPhasePlatformReceiptAuthority.phaseOne: Before loading a receipt, validate the forwarded route evidence. A command-only request must carry the exact canonical Platform Auth source scope and matching People-free receipt-route psr. A dual-qualified Work Explorer request may instead carry a fully revalidated Explorer People-derived hcm-scope and matching Explorer receipt-route psr.
twoPhasePlatformReceiptAuthority.familyRead: Only after phase one succeeds may Platform perform the tenant-and-subject-bound immutable canonical-row lookup needed to distinguish an Explorer-origin receipt from a Platform-origin receipt. This internal classification is never returned or accepted as authority; unknown IDs and every post-lookup denial return the same HTTP status and response body. R5 does not claim constant-time or equal downstream-call counts.
twoPhasePlatformReceiptAuthority.phaseTwo: For a Platform-origin row reached through the dual-qualified Explorer branch, Platform derives the canonical ORIGINATING_COMMAND_SCOPE selector and calls Auth for the exact receipt route without replaying the forwarded Explorer contextKey. Auth must derive and return the current Platform-profile contextKey from the selected scope. Platform requires one allowed hcm.command-receipt.view grant, one exact matching TARGET_POPULATION source scope, requiresProductEligibility=false, the returned canonical contextKey, current freshness and a People-null Platform receipt-route psr computed with Gateway parity. The internal Platform context and psr are retained separately and are not compared to the forwarded Explorer context or psr.
twoPhasePlatformReceiptAuthority.originProof: After phase two, re-evaluate the stored exact management origin through Auth and People, require its derived hcm-scope, authority digest, field/auth revisions, origin purpose, current origin psr and expiry, and compare every immutable seal exactly as R4 requires.
twoPhasePlatformReceiptAuthority.pepRule: The existing Platform owner PEP must still select platform-originating-command-receipt-reader from trusted Gateway permissions, roles and the typed verified receipt attribute before the controller returns the Platform projection. Shell authority alone never returns a Platform receipt.

publicAndAuthorityRevisionSplit.schema: Amend the still-unreleased V327 sys_hris_command_receipts table with authority_field_policy_revision and authority_authorization_revision BIGINT NOT NULL columns. Add both authority columns to the >0 revision check and immutable seal trigger. At the database boundary enforce each existing public revision column BETWEEN 1 AND 9007199254740991 and equal to the low-53-bit non-zero projection of its paired authority column. No V328 or backfill is permitted.
publicAndAuthorityRevisionSplit.publicProjection: Existing field_policy_revision and authorization_revision remain the public receipt values. For a trusted positive Gateway revision g, project p = g & 9007199254740991 and use 1 only when p is zero; do not rehash g. This is identical to the existing source-hash low-53-bit projection. Fixed vectors are field 4663670355146917040 -> 6948340445824176 and authorization 1991387878219104048 -> 796842921344816. The existing public DTO, JSON names, OpenAPI and frontend parser remain unchanged.
publicAndAuthorityRevisionSplit.authoritySeal: The two new authority columns store the exact positive 63-bit Gateway-parity revisions from trusted authority evidence. All current-authority comparisons use only the authority columns. Public projected revisions are display/reconciliation data and must never authorize access.
publicAndAuthorityRevisionSplit.producerRule: Explorer, reference-configuration and navigation-policy canonical receipt writers must persist both pairs atomically: JavaScript-safe values in the existing public columns and exact Gateway-parity values in the new authority columns. Existing internal authority carriers such as AuthoritySnapshot and Explorer CommandContext may retain the exact pair only; derive the public pair only at public receipt/canonical persistence boundaries. Canonical producer records keep both pairs distinct, and repository ReceiptAuthority/ReceiptActivityRow reads map authority checks to the new internal columns. Activity/provider and current-authority comparisons use the internal pair.
publicAndAuthorityRevisionSplit.responseConsistencyRule: For a newly written reference-configuration receipt, the immediate public CommandReceipt and its exact legacy replay must use the same JavaScript-safe projected values as the canonical SYS-API-038 read for that receipt ID. The exact Gateway revisions remain only in the new canonical authority columns and authority-bound digests. Navigation has no public revision fields but its canonical public pair follows the same projection rule.
publicAndAuthorityRevisionSplit.digestRule: Idempotency, request and authorization-context material must continue to bind the exact internal authority revisions, not only their public low-53-bit projections. Explorer commandDigest and any owner-provider query that currently binds the shared revision pair must include/compare the distinct exact pair so a low-53 collision cannot replay or authorize a command.
publicAndAuthorityRevisionSplit.compatibilityRule: Historical V325/V326 rows and replay are not rewritten or backfilled. Newly written legacy reference receipts receive the corrected safe public projection so their immediate response, exact replay and canonical read agree. No bigint is serialized as a new string field and no Gateway, public DTO, OpenAPI or frontend change is authorized.

privacyAndFailure.opaqueRule: Unknown ID, Explorer-only caller, command capability loss, selector mismatch, profile drift, package drift, People/Auth unavailability, psr mismatch, origin mismatch and expired evidence all return the same opaque HTTP 404 status and response body for receipt data after a tenant-and-subject-bound lookup. No constant-time guarantee or equal downstream-call-count claim is made.
privacyAndFailure.noFallbackRule: A failed exact Platform selector cannot fall back to Explorer authority, and an Explorer-origin receipt cannot be reclassified as Platform-origin.
privacyAndFailure.noClientAuthority: No new query parameter, header, profile key, role assertion or scope is accepted from the browser as owner proof.
